parts:
Hi,

the details of how to do this depends on how your covariates are
stored and what locations you want to evaluate the predictions.
The easiest case is when you have the covariates for the data
locations and the prediction locations;
use the covariate values for the data locations in the data stack, and
use the A matrix for those locations to link with the mesh, and
use the covariate values at the prediction locations in the prediction
stack, and there use the A matrix for the prediction locations to link
with the mesh.

For other situations (e.g. when you need to interpolate a covariate to
prediction locations, or even model it) it will work differently.

Finn

This gives three effects groups. I think you just need to joint all
the covariates together in one group, like this:

effects.zzz = list(c(list(Intercept = 1),
field.indices),

c(as.list(df.final.03.train1[,names.zzz]), scaled.mesh.loc))

(that's assuming the "covar" in your call was just informational and
not actually used in the formula).
